metadata.title: Stage Environment: Provisioning GCP and GitHub
metadata.source: Fellow-supplied Week 2 implementation scope (Artifact Registry, WIF trust widening, scoped IAM binding, GitHub stage Environment, validation + rollback run), provided 2026-09-17. Continues medas-frontend-cicd, medas-ci-rollback, medas-trust-chain and meddas-dev-pipeline-gcp-deployment.
metadata.description: The implementation detail of standing up a stage environment that mirrors dev exactly: a dedicated Artifact Registry repo, widening the existing Workload Identity Federation provider's trust condition (no new pool), an IAM binding scoped to the stage GitHub Environment's principal set specifically, a new GitHub stage Environment with its own secrets/variables, and two validation runs -- a real stage-v0.1.0 deploy, then a rollback against it. Implementation only; the underlying concepts (what WIF/IAM/CI-CD/Cloud Run are) are covered separately in the companion learning video, not re-explained here.
metadata.note: GitHub-dark skin throughout the body beats (diegetic subject surface, matching medas-trust-chain/medas-frontend-cicd), Claude-cream skin for the bookends (INTRO, SUMMARY, NEXT STEPS, OUTRO). Every command, variable and resource name is drawn from the fellow-supplied Week 2 scope; the attribute-mapping precondition for the scoped IAM bind (B03) is called out as a dependency, not assumed silently.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW -- Claude cream skin, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: Habari — this is Darshil. Week two of the frontend's pipeline: provisioning a stage environment that mirrors dev exactly — a new Artifact Registry repo, a widened Workload Identity trust condition, a stage-scoped IAM binding, and a new GitHub Environment — then a real tag push to validate it, and a rollback run to prove the recovery path too.

props.command: git tag stage-v0.1.0 && git push origin stage-v0.1.0
props.topic: ARTIFACT REGISTRY · WORKLOAD IDENTITY · IAM · GITHUB ENVIRONMENTS
props.segment: Stage Environment: Provisioning GCP and GitHub
props.runningText: week 2: registry → trust widening → scoped IAM → GitHub stage env → validate…
output: mirrors dev, cryptographically separated from it
two proofs required: a real deploy, then a real rollback

beats.narration_text: Step one, same shape as dev: somewhere for the staged image to live. Create a dedicated Artifact Registry repository for stage — medas-frontend-stage — in the same shared GCP project, following the existing medas-frontend naming convention, and kept distinct from the backend's medas-aggregation registries so builds never collide.

lines: --description="Docker images for medas frontend stage environment"
props.caption: stage-v* images land here; dev-v* images stay in medas-frontend-dev -- never the same namespace.

beats.role_note: step 2 -- widen the existing provider's trust condition
beats.narration_text: No new identity pool. Widen the same github-provider's trust condition so it also accepts stage-environment runs from this repo, alongside the backend and the dev environment it already trusts — one pool, now covering a third GitHub Environment.

lines: gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers update-oidc github-provider \
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers describe github-provider \
--format="value(attributeCondition)"   # <- the week-one lesson: always re-run this
props.caption: Same lesson as week one: describe after update-oidc -- never trust that it took.

beats.role_note: step 3 -- bind scoped to the stage principal set, not the whole repo
beats.narration_text: The binding this time is scoped tighter than dev's. Instead of trusting the whole repository, bind the role to the principal set for the stage GitHub Environment specifically — so a workflow run targeting dev still can't impersonate this service account through a stage-only grant, even though both environments share the one service account. That scoping only works if the provider's attribute mapping already exposes the environment claim — confirmed before writing this binding, not assumed.

lines: # confirm the provider maps the environment claim before binding to it:
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers describe github-provider \
props.caption: Dev's binding was scoped by repository; stage's is scoped by environment -- dev and stage stay cryptographically separated on one shared SA.

beats.role_note: step 4 -- new stage Environment, secrets + variables
beats.narration_text: On GitHub's side: a new Environment, stage, separate from dev. Same two secrets as dev — the provider path, the service account email. Six variables, with the three that actually differ from dev: a new repository, a new service name, and the staging backend's URL instead of dev's.

lines: # Variables -- only REPOSITORY, SERVICE and API_URL change from dev
props.caption: Same six-field shape as dev's Environment -- diff this table against dev's before the first run, don't assume it matches.

beats.role_note: step 5a -- the real stage-v0.1.0 tag push
beats.narration_text: First real test: tag stage-v0.1.0 and push it. The workflow has to resolve ENV=stage from that prefix, build with the staging API_URL baked in, push to the new registry, and deploy to a staging Cloud Run service — not dev's, not master's.

nodes.d: staging API_URL baked in, pushed to medas-frontend-stage

props.caption: Same deploy.yaml as dev and master -- only the resolved environment changes.

beats.role_note: step 5b -- rollback.yaml against that same tag, stage
beats.narration_text: Second test, same tag: run rollback.yaml once against stage-v0.1.0, with environment set to stage. If it redeploys that same image without rebuilding anything, the recovery path is proven for this environment too — not just inherited from dev by assumption. The week isn't complete until this run is green.

props.caption: A working deploy is not proof the rollback path works too -- this run is the actual proof.

beats.role_note: the lesson, one beat -- card, no new component
beats.narration_text: So here's what exists now that didn't before: an isolated stage registry, one widened trust condition instead of a second identity pool, an IAM binding scoped to the stage environment specifically, a GitHub Environment with its own secrets and variables, and two separate proofs — a real deploy and a real rollback — before calling the week complete.

props.artifactTitle: Stage Environment: Provisioning GCP and GitHub
artifactLines: Registry: medas-frontend-stage -- isolated from dev and from the backend's registries.
Trust: one WIF pool widened to a third GitHub Environment -- no new provider.
IAM: bound to the stage principal set specifically, not the whole repository.
GitHub: a new stage Environment, same two secrets, six variables with three changed.
Proven twice: a real stage-v0.1.0 deploy, then a real rollback against it.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW -- suggested prompt, read and discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn: before granting a new environment's principal access to a service account it already shares with another environment, check whether the identity provider's attribute mapping actually exposes the claim you plan to scope by — environment, not just repository — before you write the binding, not after it fails.
